4.1.2 Recreation
In order to maintain the integrity of the proposed hiking trail and related features for public use, the Applicant would continue to refrain from harvesting timber within most of the trail corridor, including the existing natural areas at Windy Falls and Coon Branch. However, the Applicant proposes to reserve the right to alter, discontinue, or relocate all or a portion of the proposed trail as needs may require, with the advice of the Foothills Trail Conference, Inc., whose membership includes several State and Federal agencies and interested local organizations and individuals.
4.2 ENVIRONMENTAL RESTORATION AND ENHANCEMENT
The planned environmental restoration program includes measures to prevent additional siltation of Howard Creek, but the Applicant acknowledges the probable occurrence of adverse conditions initially during periods of high runoff. Rehabilitation measures would be implemented as soon as practical, but the restoration of Howard Creek would depend primarily upon the cleansing action of natural stream processes.
After cuts and fills are completed, slopes would be seeded with a grass-legume mixture as soon as practical, and adequate drainage would be provided. Temporary roads would be regraded and planted with seedlings or seeded with a grass-legume mixture when no longer needed. The permanent access road would be paved as soon as practical. Riprap would be used to control erosion in areas where other measures fail. The Applicant has stated that Howard Creek above Highway 171 would not be affected, since the borrow site now identified would be relocated east of Highway 171.
Riprap material would be used on both faces of the Bad Creek dam to control erosion. The Applicant plans to mitigate the adverse visual impact of a flutuating pumped storage reservoir by providing adequate natural screening to minimize the view of the reservoir from the public highways and overlooks.
